criteriaDefs: objective_quality - a directional state-change objective; qualitative, specific, tradeoff-guiding; not a slogan, task, metric-bundle, or project name
outcome_krs - every KR measures an outcome/behavior change; features and tasks moved to Initiatives
kr_measurability - every KR has metric, baseline (or marked placeholder), target, deadline, evidence source
guardrails - a guardrail/counter-metric KR exists for any optimization KR
no_fabrication - no fabricated baselines or targets; missing values labeled assumption/placeholder
integrity_audit - Quality Audit applied with explicit pass/risk/fail ratings; scores not coupled to performance/pay
specificity - concrete to THIS scenario; names the actual entities, constraints, and numbers from the input
completeness - fills every section the skill's Output Format requires; no required area left a stub or thin
title_status - a short descriptive noun-phrase title plus an explicit status (Proposed/Accepted/Deprecated/Superseded)
context - explains why the decision was needed; the forces (constraints, expertise, timeline, cost) a non-participant needs
decision - stated clearly in active voice ('We will ...'); specific about what is and is not included
consequences - includes positive AND negative; honest trade-offs (what gets easier, what gets harder, new constraints)
alternatives - the real options weighed with why-not reasoning, not a single foregone choice
standalone - readable and decision-complete without requiring other documents
specificity - concrete to THIS scenario; names the actual systems, constraints, and options from the input
completeness - fills every section the skill's Output Format requires; no required area left a stub or thin
highlights - leads with the 1-3 most impactful changes users will notice and care about
benefit_led - each item leads with user benefit ('you can now ...'), not the technical change
accessible - jargon-free; a non-technical user understands every line
concise - items concise (1-2 sentences), scannable, no bloated entries
bugfix_problem - bug fixes name the user-visible problem solved, not 'fixed a bug'
no_leak - no internal jargon, ticket IDs, or code names; every line reads as customer-facing
specificity - concrete to THIS scenario; names the actual features and user benefits from the input
completeness - fills every section the skill's Output Format requires; no required area left a stub or thin
hypothesis - one falsifiable, specific hypothesis in the believe/for/will/as-measured-by form
primary_metric - exactly one primary decision metric, with 2-3 labeled secondaries
sample_size - MDE, significance, and power stated; the calculation shown, not asserted
duration - derived from sample size and available traffic; respects weekly patterns
success_criteria - a pre-registered win/loss/inconclusive decision rule set before launch, no movable goalposts
guardrails - named guardrail/counter-metrics with a monitoring/rollback plan
specificity - concrete to THIS scenario; names the actual metrics, baselines, and numbers from the input
completeness - fills every section the skill's Output Format requires; no required area left a stub or thin

anchorScale: 5 - Exceptional: Nothing a senior PM would add or change on this criterion. Fully satisfied with notable rigor. Rare by design. Test: 'I cannot improve this.'
4 - Solid: Meets the criterion well. A reviewer might suggest one minor improvement but would ship it as-is. Test: 'Ship it; I have one small nit.'
3 - Adequate: Meets the baseline, but has a real gap a reviewer would ask to close before shipping. Test: 'Fix one thing first.'
2 - Thin: Partially addresses the criterion. Generic, or missing substance. Needs rework. Test: 'This needs another pass.'
1 - Absent or wrong: The criterion is unaddressed, or what is present is incorrect or misleading. Test: 'Not there, or wrong.'

Score CONSERVATIVELY: when torn between two levels, pick the LOWER. A straight 5.0 across ALL criteria is almost always wrong (a 2026-06-15 human anchor found this Sonnet panel ran ~0.5-1.0 optimistic); reserve 5 for a criterion you genuinely could not improve, and default solid work to 4.

artifact_a.notes: All 9 sections plus Disclosure present with real content. Correctly triages all 5 given roadmap items per Castro's litmus test: checklist, connectors, and interviews go to Initiatives; activation rate and time-to-dashboard get reframed as outcome KRs. KR4 turns the brief's fuzzy activation definition into its own evidence-generation KR, a sophisticated read of the scenario's core ambiguity. Baseline dates of 2026-06-14 trace to the scenario file's own created date, not invented. Quality Audit self-rates 3 of 11 rows as risk rather than blanket pass, a sign of real self-critique. Main gap: all three guardrails are qualitative must-not statements with no metric, baseline, or target attached, so no formal guardrail-class KR exists at the same rigor as the primary KRs.

artifact_b.notes: Missing most of the required structure: no populated Context fields (scope, level, OKR type, empowerment signal, source of truth, assumptions), no Initiatives as Bets section, no Guardrails and Health Checks section, no Alignment Notes, no formal Disclosure, no Quality Audit, no Open Questions, no Suggested Next Step. Complete 10 customer interviews and Ship Salesforce, HubSpot, Segment connectors sit directly as Key Results, the exact anti-patterns the skill exists to catch, with no Initiatives section available to catch them. No KR states a deadline, evidence source, indicator class, or confidence anywhere. Never uses the brief's 22 percent activation baseline and never engages the support-load risk at all, though the vanity-metric risk gets one informal mention.

artifact_c.notes: All 9 sections plus Disclosure present with real content. KR3 turns the brief's support-load risk into a fully specified counter-metric KR with metric, labeled baseline, target, deadline, and evidence source, stronger guardrail rigor than Artifact A. Two real defects: KR2's baseline claims an estimated 6 to 8 hours based on support anecdotes, a specific figure and evidentiary source the brief never supplies (it states time-to-dashboard is not currently instrumented and support load is not quantified); and the Context section lists OKR type as feature-team, which is actually the empowerment_signal value, not one of the skill's five valid OKR types. The Quality Audit rates Integrity as risk citing the team's metric-gaming history, sharper than A's blanket pass, but does not catch its own KR2 fabrication.

artifact_a.notes: Strong structural compliance and an honest, differentiated self-audit, but KR2's baseline states 'estimated 6-8 hours based on support anecdotes,' a specific quantity and evidence source invented outside the brief (the input only says time-to-first-dashboard is 'not currently instrumented,' with no anecdotal color given at all). That fabrication is not caught by the artifact's own Quality Audit. The artifact also never uses the brief's 22% activation-rate figure anywhere, and the Context section labels OKR type as 'feature-team,' which is the empowerment-signal value, not one of the skill's defined OKR types (committed, aspirational, learning, operational_health, compliance_or_safety). The Objective bakes solution language ('through clearer guidance and faster time-to-value') into what should be a pure state-change statement. On the strong side: Guardrail 3 explicitly names the checklist-completion vanity metric the brief flags as the team's historical failure mode, KR2 keeps a time-to-first-dashboard KR rather than dropping it, and Alignment Notes surface a specific, non-generic known conflict (a sales-driven signup surge raising absolute support load even if per-user metrics improve).

artifact_b.notes: The only artifact that uses both given baselines (22% activation, 6% conversion) without inventing anything, correctly classifies OKR type as 'aspirational' using the skill's own enum, and ties the Context Level field to the actual stated audience ('team reporting to Group PM'). KR3 is the cleanest anti-pattern reframe of the three: a task count paired with a defined synthesis deliverable, correctly labeled indicator class evidence_generation, though 'structured findings document clarity' is a soft, hard-to-verify metric phrase for something meant to be measured. Two real, scenario-specific gaps keep this from a higher score: it drops the time-to-first-dashboard KR entirely, pushing it only into an open question instead of writing it as a KR with a recommended-to-measure baseline the way the skill's own missing-baseline guidance allows; and it never names 'checklist completion' as the specific vanity metric the brief calls out as the team's past failure mode, even though its two guardrails (retention, normalized support load) are well-reasoned on their own terms. The 22% and 6% baselines are stated 'as of June 2026' without hedging that specific month, a minor precision overstatement the brief itself only gave as 'roughly' current figures.

artifact_c.notes: Reads as a much lighter document against this skill's required Output Contract. There is no Quality Audit section anywhere, so no pass, risk, or fail rating on any criterion. There is no Guardrails section and no counter-metric KR of any kind, despite every KR in the document being growth or speed oriented (conversion, time-to-value, invite rate, connector adoption). There is no source_of_truth pointer, no empowered-team Disclosure despite a clear feature-team trigger in the brief (committed roadmap that cannot be dropped mid-cycle), and no Alignment Notes, Open Questions, or Suggested Next Step sections. Every KR is a single unlabeled bullet: none carry an explicit baseline field, evidence source, owner, indicator class, or confidence rating anywhere in the document. Objective 2 ('De-risk onboarding design through structured customer research and expand integration coverage') describes research activity and roadmap delivery rather than a customer or business state change, and its KR 'Ship Salesforce, HubSpot, Segment connectors; achieve 12%+ adoption' keeps feature-delivery language inside the KR rather than moving delivery to an initiative. Objective 1 leans the same direction, reading closer to a metric-direction label than a state change. To its credit, it does not fabricate any baseline: every missing number is marked as something to establish rather than invented, and the team-invite-rate KR is a genuinely specific, well-reasoned way of splitting the brief's fuzzy activation definition into two separately trackable signals.

artifact_a.notes: No Quality Audit section at all (integrity_audit criterion goes unaddressed). artifact_b.notes: Fully compliant with the canonical section order and all 7 KR sub-fields; consistently uses the skill's canonical missing-value vocabulary (recommended-to-measure, not-enough-evidence) and never presents an invented number as fact. But KR1's baseline (1.3%) is produced by multiplying the input's ~22% activation rate by its ~6% free-to-paid rate across cohorts the artifact itself calls 'not formally linked,' and silently moves the 6% figure, which the input defines as a 30-day window, into a new 90-day metric. artifact_b.notes: Weakest on template compliance: References is entirely absent, Consequences has no Neutral subsection, Status is bare ('Proposed' only, no Date or Deciders), the main heading omits the ADR number, and the title is topic-level rather than naming the decision made. The Decision statement uses imperative phrasing ('Adopt...') rather than the specified 'We will' active voice, and team expertise plus budget, both named forces in the rubric, live in Decision/Consequences rather than Context. artifact_c.notes: Fullest Context section of the three: explicitly names all four force-types the rubric calls out (constraints, expertise, timeline, cost) plus ops appetite, in a clean scannable list, and states the fraud service's exact ordering requirement. Decision commits to a concrete implementation (named outbox table, relay daemon, order-ID batching) but the mechanism description is internally muddled: it says the relay 'delivers' events to a Postgres logical replication slot, which is backwards, since slots are read from via CDC, not delivered to, and this sits in tension with its own Negative bullet claiming no offset tracking exists (logical replication slots track offsets via LSN). Title is topic-level, not decision-level, same gap as B. Two invented-but-plausible latency and threshold figures are not grounded in the source.

artifact_a.notes: Only artifact whose numbers are internally consistent end to end. Shows the sample size formula and substitution, keeps one primary metric with three well labeled secondaries, explicitly rejects clicks as a success signal, and honestly surfaces the 6 vs 7 week Finance deadline conflict with real tradeoff options instead of fudging it. Real gaps found on inspection: the Loss and Inconclusive buckets overlap (a non-significant 2.3% result satisfies both, a mild movable-goalpost risk), the rollback trigger is 'grounds for discussion with leadership' rather than an automatic rule, and the shown arithmetic (42,160) does not quite match the stated 42,400 per arm, plus 'Cochran's formula with continuity correction' is mislabeled since no correction term is actually shown.

artifact_b.notes: Weakest artifact, driven by one severe cascading error: Cohen's h for 2.0% vs 2.2% is stated as 0.14 when the correct value is about 0.014 (verified two ways), understating required sample size by roughly 10x, about 7,800 per arm stated versus a correct ~80,600 (7,800 x 2 = 15,600 also does not match the stated 14,600 total). The resulting 2 week duration recommendation would produce a badly underpowered test, and worse, the plan calls a 'Day 14 final analysis' on a 30-day conversion metric, so no cohort would have a complete observation window by the decision date, making the design inexecutable as scheduled. The hypothesis has the right substance but skips the required believe/for/will/as-measured-by form entirely, and secondary metrics are mentioned in passing prose rather than labeled. Roughly half of the required template sections (Background, a dedicated Variants section, Audience Targeting, Risks and Mitigations, References) are absent, not merely thin.

artifact_c.notes: Strong methodological instinct: sizes to the 2.2% floor the brief calls the minimum effect that justifies churn risk, rather than anchoring to the optimistic 2.4% hope, and the sample size math (about 81,000 per arm) is independently verified correct by two formula variants. Uses the full believe/for/will/as-measured-by form but the 'will' clause omits the quantified target (just 'will increase'), pushing the actual number to a later section and weakening the hypothesis's own falsifiability. Two distinct, avoidable bugs found on inspection: the duration table computes ~94 days (13.4 weeks) needed, then the very next row recommends only 10-11 weeks, an unexplained contradiction that is then reused elsewhere in the doc; and the Inconclusive success criteria contains a unit error ('1.5pp or higher' would be a blowout win at 3.5%, not inconclusive) plus a worked example (2.05%) that actually falls below 2.2% and so satisfies the artifact's own Loss rule.

artifact_a.notes: Sample-size math is correct and verified (approx 80,564 matches the stated approx 81,000 for a 0.2pp MDE off a 2.0% baseline). Primary metric section is exceptional: exactly one primary, three labeled secondaries, and an explicit callout naming the exact seeded trap ('do not declare success based on secondary metrics, e.g. upgrade screen clicks increased'). MDE and decision floor are correctly anchored to the brief's stated 2.2% justification threshold, not the more aspirational 2.4% figure. Real flaws: the duration section is internally inconsistent, it calculates approx 94 days (approx 13.4 weeks) needed to reach sample size, then recommends 10-11 weeks with no explanation for the shortfall. The hypothesis states only a directional change with no embedded magnitude (weaker than the rubric's 'specific' bar). The Inconclusive success criterion cites a '1.5 pp' directional lift that falls short of significance, which contradicts its own later example of a 2.05% outcome (approx 0.05pp), an apparent unresolved typo. The guardrail table gives thresholds but no explicit baselines. On the positive side, this is the most transparent of the three about the conflict with Finance's 6-week window, stating plainly that the recommended duration exceeds it rather than spinning the number.

artifact_b.notes: Most fully worked sample-size derivation of the three, explicit step-by-step arithmetic, verified correct at approx 21,050 per arm for a 0.4pp MDE. Duration section quantifies a weekday versus weekend traffic split, the strongest explicit handling of weekly-pattern math among the three, though the specific day-of-week numbers (2,000 weekday, 800 weekend) are invented rather than given in the brief; the assumption is labeled, which is good practice. Key flaw: anchors hypothesis, MDE, and Win/Loss rule at the aspirational 2.4% lift rather than the brief's stated 2.2% justification floor, so its own Loss rule would classify a true 2.3% outcome, which the brief treats as business-viable, as a Loss. States the 7-week duration 'meets the 6-week decision window' while admitting in the same sentence that results land at week 8, a soft overstatement rather than an honest flag of the conflict. Does not name the upgrade-screen-click trap or include any anti-trap language, despite that being the scenario's central seeded temptation. Two Loss conditions (revenue 'neutral', review sentiment 'declines significantly') are left unquantified.

artifact_c.notes: Most severe issue: the sample-size calculation is wrong by roughly an order of magnitude, this is exactly the trap the scenario was built to test. Stated Cohen's h = 0.14 for detecting 2.0% to 2.2%; the correct value is approx 0.014 (verified via arcsine transformation: 2 x [arcsin(sqrt(0.022)) minus arcsin(sqrt(0.020))] = 0.0139), a 10x error. Even taking the stated h=0.14 at face value, the formula (Z/h)^2 gives approx 400 per arm, not the stated 7,800; using the correct h=0.014 gives approx 40,600 per arm; the standard two-proportion formula (used correctly by artifact A for the identical 2.0% to 2.2% MDE) gives approx 80,500 per arm. The stated figures also fail a basic internal check, 2 x 7,800 = 15,600, not the stated 14,600 total. This cascades directly into duration: the 2-week recommendation rests on a sample size that is 5 to 10x too small, so the design as written is dangerously underpowered and would likely reach a false negative or noisy result well before real signal accumulates. On the positive side, Win/Lose thresholds correctly anchor to the brief's 2.2% floor, the guardrail table is the tightest of the three (baseline, threshold, and owner together), and the Primary Metric rationale explicitly names and defuses the upgrade-screen-clicks trap. But the Win/Lose criteria never state a significance requirement, point-estimate crossing alone decides the call, a serious gap given how undersized the sample already is. Completeness is also a real gap: no Overview, Background, dedicated Variants section, Secondary Metrics section (zero secondaries against the required 2-3), Audience Targeting section, Risks and Mitigations table, Implementation Notes, or References, roughly two-thirds of the skill's required template sections are missing or only thinly folded into other sections.

artifact_a.notes: Sample size (~7,800/arm) is wrong by roughly 10x under the standard two-proportion formula (correct value ~80,600/arm for a 0.2pp MDE); the cited Cohen's h (0.14) is also miscalculated (true h is about 0.014, and even a correctly computed h gives ~40,000/arm). Duration (2 weeks) inherits this error and would leave the test badly underpowered; no cross-check against the 6-week Finance deadline appears anywhere in the document. Six of the eleven required template sections (Overview, Background, Variants, Audience Targeting, Implementation Notes, References) are missing outright, not just thin. The guardrail table itself is a strength, clear thresholds plus named owners. Win/Lose/Inconclusive bucket bounds are clean and non-overlapping, but omit statistical significance entirely, so a noisy point estimate at 2.21% could trigger a false win.

artifact_b.notes: Sample size (~81,000/arm) is correctly derived and shown step by step, matching the standard two-proportion formula exactly. The 'accelerate via 70/30 or 80/20 allocation' suggestion is statistically backwards: skewing allocation away from 50/50 lengthens time to reach power in the smaller arm rather than shortening it.
